_comment: Ollama — a SEPARATE server for the Telegram Support Suite's AI. The suite talks to it over HTTP at AI_BASE_URL (http://<this server>:<port>/v1). Pulls BOTH a chat model and an embedding model: the suite needs the embedding model to match questions by meaning and to reuse answers for repeat questions, and without it the bot silently falls back to keyword matching.
name: Ollama (for Telegram Support Suite)
author: support-suite@localhost
description: Standalone Ollama LLM server. Binds 0.0.0.0:<port>, auto-pulls a chat model and an embedding model on first start, and keeps them resident so a quiet group does not pay a model reload on every question. Allocate ~8GB RAM and ~8GB disk for a 3B model; more for larger ones.
startup: bash -c 'export OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0:{{SERVER_PORT}}; export OLLAMA_MODELS=/home/container/.ollama/models; export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/home/container/lib/ollama; export OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE="${OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE:--1}"; export OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH="${OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH:-8192}"; export OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL=1; export OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=2; /home/container/bin/ollama serve & SRV=$!; until curl -s http://127.0.0.1:{{SERVER_PORT}}/api/tags >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done; for M in "$OLLAMA_MODEL" "$OLLAMA_EMBED_MODEL"; do [ -n "$M" ] && { /home/container/bin/ollama list | grep -q "^$M[[:space:]]" || { echo "[ollama] pulling $M ..."; /home/container/bin/ollama pull "$M"; }; }; done; echo "[ollama] models ready: $(/home/container/bin/ollama list | tail -n +2 | awk '"'"'{print $1}'"'"' | tr '"'"'\n'"'"' '"'"' '"'"')"; wait $SRV'

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Ollama for the Telegram Support Suite — its own server, reached over HTTP.
# The suite never runs the model in-process; point AI_BASE_URL at this server.
set -euo pipefail
log() { echo "[Ollama] $*"; }

log "Installing tooling..."
apt update -y
apt install -y --no-install-recommends curl ca-certificates tar zstd

mkdir -p /mnt/server/.ollama/models
cd /mnt/server

# The bundled CUDA/ROCm libraries are the bulk of the ~1.4GB archive and are
# dead weight on a CPU node. Excluding them is the default BUT it is a choice,
# not a fact about the egg: a server installed this way can never use a GPU,
# however the node is later upgraded. Set OLLAMA_SKIP_GPU_LIBS=0 and reinstall
# to get them back.
EXCLUDES=()
if [ "${OLLAMA_SKIP_GPU_LIBS:-1}" = "1" ]; then
  log "CPU-only install: excluding bundled GPU libraries (~110MB instead of ~1.4GB)."
  EXCLUDES=('--exclude=lib/ollama/cuda*' '--exclude=lib/ollama/rocm*')
else
  log "Including GPU libraries — only worth it if this node actually has a GPU."
fi

log "Downloading + extracting Ollama..."
curl -fSL "https://ollama.com/download/ollama-linux-amd64.tar.zst" \
  | tar --use-compress-program=unzstd -xf - -C /mnt/server ${EXCLUDES[@]+"${EXCLUDES[@]}"}

if [ ! -x /mnt/server/bin/ollama ]; then
  echo "[Ollama] ERROR: ollama binary missing after extraction."
  echo "[Ollama] Check the server's Disk limit — the binary needs ~150MB and each model several GB on top."
  exit 1
fi

log "Install complete. Models are pulled on first start, not here."

variables.name: Chat model
variables.description: The model that writes answers. On a CPU node this is your single biggest speed lever: a 3B (qwen2.5:3b, llama3.2:3b) generates roughly 3x faster than an 8B and answers support questions well, because the suite feeds it the relevant FAQs rather than relying on what the model knows. Use llama3.1:8b or qwen2.5:7b only if the node has cores and RAM to spare. Avoid gemma* on CPU — it re-reads the whole prompt every message.

variables.name: Embedding model
variables.description: Used to match questions by meaning and to reuse answers for repeat questions. Cheap even on CPU — embedding a question is one pass, not a generated answer. Leave empty to disable, and the suite falls back to keyword matching.

variables.name: Keep models loaded
variables.description: How long an idle model stays in memory. -1 means never unload, which is what you want: Ollama's own default of 5m makes a quiet group pay a full model reload on top of prompt reading for nearly every question. Set e.g. 10m only if RAM is tight.

variables.name: Context length
variables.description: Tokens of context. The suite's support prompt plus retrieved FAQs runs to a few thousand tokens, and Ollama's smaller default would truncate it mid-template and return a 500.

variables.name: CPU-only install (skip GPU libraries)
variables.description: 1 = skip the bundled CUDA/ROCm libraries, cutting the install from ~1.4GB to ~110MB. Correct for a CPU node, but a server installed this way can never use a GPU — set to 0 and reinstall if the node has one.
